title: How the UK's hottest summer has affected autumn leaves
summary:
This year's display of autumn leaves could look rather different following the UK's hottest summer on record.
Months of heat and drought have put trees under stress, causing some to shed their leaves earlier than usual in a phenomenon known as a "false autumn".
Experts say this could mean a more varied display of autumn colours, with some trees losing their leaves prematurely while others are yet to change colour.
However, some trees could still produce spectacular shades of red, orange and gold.

title: Climate Change Committee chair on Northern Ireland fact-finding mission
summary:
"Courage and leadership" are needed to ensure Northern Ireland catches up on tackling climate change.
The new chair of the Climate Change Committee, Nigel Topping, is spending two days on a fact-finding mission to hear the thoughts of people across different sectors.
He said Northern Ireland was a small nation that could be "agile and innovative" in tackling challenges like increasing renewable energy, improving waste management and reducing emissions.
It is being described as a fact-finding mission, looking at "challenges and opportunities".
He acknowledged that politics in Northern Ireland was "complex" and that "when things flip-flop, it doesn't help", due to the impact on investment decisions and people's choices.

title: The Greenest Cities in America, Ranked
summary:
Going green is no longer just a buzzword, but the blueprint for modern city living.
The clean, green capitals of the United States prove that maintaining a sustainable city is a symbiotic process that doesn't have to involve sacrificing comfort or convenience.
In America's greenest city, "green" isn't merely a metaphor—it's the literal color of the landscape when you take in all of Oakland's lush parks.

title: Volunteers plant 109,000 trees in new Lancashire woodlands
summary:
New woodlands have been created by volunteers planting more than 109,000 trees across Lancashire in the last year.
In the last two tree-planting seasons, the Lancashire Woodland Partnership has planted almost 500,000 trees and more than 27,233 metres of new hedges.
Lancashire County Councillor Joshua Roberts said the woodlands were "supporting wildlife, helping tackle climate change, improving people's wellbeing".
The partnership brings together environmental organisations, local authorities, landowners, volunteers and communities to combine resources, expertise and local knowledge.
The organisations then plant trees where they can deliver the greatest benefits for wildlife, people and the environment.
